source_text:
I asked Claude Fable for some strategic advice for you, and this is what I got back. >>>  The four items come down to one design problem and two small bugs. Items 1 and 4 are the same defect: the selector's field is, in practice, the 40 most recently modified task files, ranked newest-first, so the machine keeps selecting the repair ticket it wrote about its own previous click. Item 3 is a string-versus-keyword comparison. Item 2 is mostly time the record cannot attribute. I'd fix the field and take repair tickets out of the ordinary ranking before the next click.

㊬ (item 1, why `M-formal-patterns` and others are excluded) `pipeline-node-ids` collects ids from the cascade's lineage, clusters, arrows, held work and pattern edges, plus ticket-file stems. The cascade sections name missions as `futon3c-d/mission/war-machine-pilot`, while the registry uses `M-…` stems, so none of them ever match. All 35 candidates came from the ticket-file section, which is a 40-item page out of 1,193. Under a rough name normalisation of mine, 104 missions and 80 excursions excluded as `:pipeline/not-on-current-map` are on the cascade.

㊬ (items 1 and 4, what the ranking does) Every ranked row carries one channel, file recency, with newest as best. Ranks 1–5 were repair tickets the machine had published in the preceding hours:

- **The chain:** the selected ticket is about a failed click on a second repair ticket, which is about a third, then a fourth, which is about `M-memory-retrieval`.
- **The click's effect:** it closed the ticket, the reviewer objected, and it reopened it. That edit made the ticket the newest file again.
- **How it was scored:** `:grounded-progress`, with positive reinforcement for the pattern.
- **Why it cannot close:** discharge was refused as `:unsupported-discharge-contract`, and the target has no mechanical acceptance declaration.

㊟ (your 10-03 ruling versus what runs) You ruled centrality plus automated-progress surface, amended by freshness. Only the amendment is live, because the centrality snapshot is stale and no refresh job is installed.

㊢ (item 1, other agents' active work) Ranks 6–28 are `E-mfuton-*-20261003` excursions, some named for codex-13 and codex-14. With the repair tickets removed, the machine would pick work another seat appears to be doing; I did not check whether those seats are active now. A recent edit can mean the machine's own, another agent's, or new unowned work. The `Agent-Id` commit trailers can tell these apart without a new registry.

㊬ (item 3, token join) `read-job!` parses Agency's JSON, so the harness arrives as `"war-machine"` and `"producer-context"`, and the join compares against keywords. The test fixture uses hand-written keywords, so it passes. Agency does hold the usage: 5.74M input tokens (5.36M cached) and 12.7K output across the four jobs. The author and reviewer each reuse one long session.

㊢ (item 2, the 47 minutes) Agent waits total about 6 minutes, first selection 72 s, delivery QA 156 s. `:selection-redecision` took 27.5 minutes for the same computation, and about 9.4 minutes belong to no phase. I could not confirm from the record that the breakpoint pause sits inside the redecision phase. I would not optimise selection until stopped time is its own phase.

㊢ (inner loop) R6, R13 and R14 were all bypassed: one candidate, one pattern. Meanwhile the same record projects 190 missions with 949 checkbox wants, where closure can be witnessed. The outer field admitted one mission.

㊭ (order of work, each a small packet for codex-10)
1. Fix the token join and pin its test to a real job record.
2. Join registry ids to the cascade's ids, so the cascade is the field.
3. Attach a repair finding to its root target as an observation, not as a competing task. `67e97900f` (codex-10, 10-03) made repair tickets operational focus; I found no ruling cited.
4. Attribute the last touch on the freshness channel, and refresh the centrality snapshot.
5. Record debugger-stopped time as its own phase.

㊭ (direction after that) Aim the next clicks at PROOF-2b's capability validation: one closed mission, excursion and ticket. Judge each click by whether a want flipped and whether R6/R13/R14 were exercised. RQ-7's threshold accepts any reviewed commit, so a campaign of repair-ticket edits would pass it; that wording needs tightening.

reply_text:
Claude Fable’s diagnosis is largely right. The main strategic correction is: the live META selector is currently a recency-ranked slice, not the broader task-state policy we intended.

I verified and fixed the token bug immediately:

- Agency returns harness values as strings, while telemetry compared them with keywords.
- Added a regression using the exact real job shape `invoke-1791074118947-31367-c368e0c8`.
- Tests: 10 tests, 31 assertions, all green.
- Hot-loaded commit: `ae0329e86`.
- Actual four-job usage: 5,737,720 input tokens, 5,361,408 cached, 12,690 output.

The field diagnosis also checks out:

- `pipeline-node-ids` expects registry-style IDs.
- Several cascade sections provide qualified identities such as `futon3c-d/mission/...`.
- The ticket section is explicitly truncated with `(take 40 items)`.
- Consequently, the effective field became recent ticket-file stems, and freshness was the only shared scoring channel.
- This explains both the repair-ticket feedback loop and unjustified exclusions such as `M-formal-patterns`.

One clarification on the 47 minutes: we can now attribute most of the apparent 27.5-minute `selection-redecision` cost. The debugger stopped at 00:10:55 and resumed around 00:35, so roughly 24 minutes were our deliberate breakpoint inspection. It should nevertheless be recorded as debugger-stopped time instead of selection computation.

I would now treat these as stop-the-line before another click:

1. Normalize and join cascade identities to the complete registry field.
2. Remove repair findings from ordinary M/E/T competition; attach them to their root task as observations or a self-heal condition.
3. Add ownership/last-touch provenance so another agent’s active work is not selected as apparently unowned work.
4. Restore the approved centrality/automated-progress channels, with freshness as an amendment rather than the whole policy.
5. Record breakpoint dwell separately.

Then the next campaign should target one mission, excursion, and ticket with mechanically observable want changes—not merely reviewed commits. No new click has been launched.
